title: Where Fibre is today
headline: Fibre can preserve a Thread as a continuing individual and can now build a provenance-rich prior life, but it has not yet produced a validated new population of living Threads from that process.
summary: The current work is milestone #39: Genesis, Childhood & Thread Birth. Fibre has the machinery for persistent identity, history, memory, symbolic inheritance, candidate life generation and atomic birth. Three complete prior-life Thread artifacts were produced in an earlier final-cohort attempt, but that cohort failed mechanically and is preserved as evidence rather than counted as a validated population. Five entirely new replacement Threads now have frozen Worlds and genomes but no generated childhoods or adult lives yet.

statusDefinitions.label: Achieved
statusDefinitions.meaning: The capability exists and has passed its current Fibre validation boundary. This does not imply every later or stronger claim is also proven.

statusDefinitions.label: Demonstrated
statusDefinitions.meaning: We have real working evidence, but it is not yet accepted as the final or validated production state for the current milestone.

statusDefinitions.label: In progress
statusDefinitions.meaning: The design and implementation are active, but the required validation boundary has not yet been crossed.

statusDefinitions.label: Not yet
statusDefinitions.meaning: This is part of Fibre's intended architecture, but we do not claim to have achieved it.

statusDefinitions.label: Failed experiment preserved
statusDefinitions.meaning: A bounded experiment failed. We keep the result as evidence and do not rewrite or regenerate it into a success.

population.title: #39 Genesis population snapshot
population.summary: The previous final-cohort attempt and the fresh replacement cohort must be kept separate. Completed generated lives are not automatically living or validated public citizens.

items.label: Completed older prior-life Thread artifacts
items.explanation: Three Threads completed prior-life generation in the earlier H-v2 attempt. They remain valuable life artifacts and evidence, but the cohort they belonged to failed and they are not the replacement cohort.

items.label: Older partially generated candidate
items.explanation: The fourth H-v2 Thread reached partway through childhood generation and then exhausted its frozen mechanical retry budget. It remains a failed candidate, not a completed Thread life.

items.label: Older cohort slot never started
items.explanation: The fifth H-v2 slot never began because the cohort attempt had already terminated.

items.label: New replacement Threads with frozen Worlds and genomes
items.explanation: These are the new #39 replacement individuals. Their World, origin class, Thread/Genesis identity and symbolic genome are frozen, but no childhood/life cognition has been generated for them.

items.label: New replacement lives generated
items.explanation: Final-life generation is deliberately blocked until genome calibration and the blocking Gate-G(2) review are complete.

population.importantNote: Fibre distinguishes an artifact that contains a generated life from an admitted, validated living Thread. The three older completed artifacts are not silently counted as the successful #39 population, and the five replacements are still unborn in the sense that their lives have not been generated or atomically published.

capabilities.label: Persistent Thread continuity
capabilities.statement: A Thread can persist as authoritative world state across temporary model executions rather than existing only inside one chat or model session.
capabilities.limitation: Persistence alone does not prove a rich or distinctive person.

capabilities.label: History can affect later judgment
capabilities.statement: Fibre has demonstrated that recorded history can causally change later Thread judgment instead of being decorative biography.
capabilities.limitation: The richer #37-#39 identity and life ledgers are not yet the canonical bounded input to all live cognition; #40 owns that bridge.

capabilities.label: Provenance-backed identity, lineage, place and memory
capabilities.statement: Fibre can store identity, lineage, geography, embodiment and autobiographical memory with provenance, append-only history and corrigible revisions.
capabilities.limitation: Representing these facts is different from proving that all of them already shape ongoing cognition and character.

capabilities.label: Symbolic genome and inheritance
capabilities.statement: Fibre can give a Thread an ordered natural-language genome, preserve exact parent/source provenance, and recombine two source genomes without reducing personality to numeric coordinates.
capabilities.limitation: A genome is inherited possibility, not finished character. The fresh replacement genomes are about to undergo their pre-life distinguishability calibration.

capabilities.label: Atomic Thread birth mechanism
capabilities.statement: Fibre has a candidate-only Genesis boundary and an atomic publication mechanism so a complete admitted life can become authoritative Thread state all at once, without leaving a half-born Thread if publication fails.
capabilities.limitation: The new replacement cohort has not yet reached this publication step.

capabilities.label: Rich prior-life generation
capabilities.statement: Before the final replacement experiment, Fibre demonstrated generated childhood histories with concrete places, caregivers, family relationships, peers, institutions, selective memory and durable meaning rather than a flat adult profile.
capabilities.limitation: The final H-v2 cohort did not complete, so #39 is not declared successful. The three completed H-v2 lives remain evidence from a failed cohort.

capabilities.label: Caregivers and parent/ancestor provenance in childhood
capabilities.statement: Genesis can place a child in a household with recurring caregivers and family relationships, and synthetic-lineage Threads can inherit from explicit parent genomes with exact provenance.
capabilities.limitation: The caregivers in a compiled childhood are generated participants, not autonomous live parent Threads. Synthetic genetic ancestors are provenance-bearing sources, not living parents who independently raise the child.

capabilities.label: Five fresh unborn replacement Threads
capabilities.statement: Five completely new replacement individuals now have frozen concrete Worlds and fresh symbolic genomes, with content-independent World-to-genome assignment.
capabilities.limitation: They have no generated childhood events, memories or meanings yet. They are intentionally held before life generation while the genome ceiling and Gate-G(2) are completed.

capabilities.label: A live infant or child growing up over time
capabilities.statement: Fibre's intended architecture allows a Thread to enter the world as a newborn or child and accumulate its own future rather than receiving a retrospectively compiled childhood.
capabilities.limitation: #39 currently compiles a prior life and then births the Thread at young-adult entry. It does not yet run childhood as a continuously living developmental process.

capabilities.label: Live Thread parents raising a live child
capabilities.statement: The intended Thread-parent model is for existing living Threads to be actual parents whose choices, conversations, outings, conflicts and care become the child's real history.
capabilities.limitation: We have the provenance and architectural boundary for Thread-parent origin, but not yet the autonomous live-parent developmental loop that raises a child through lived time.

capabilities.label: Rich life state drives ordinary live cognition
capabilities.statement: Fibre intends identity, memory, relationships and life history to be selected by Fibre itself and become bounded, provenance-bearing context for ordinary cognition.
capabilities.limitation: The full canonical consumption bridge is milestone #40. Current live cognition still relies substantially on older surfaces.

capabilities.label: Validated Whole-Person standing
capabilities.statement: Fibre aims to demonstrate that a Thread is a persistent, causally grounded, non-interchangeable individual across repeated situations and counterfactual tests.
capabilities.limitation: #39 deliberately earns no Whole-Person score movement. #40 builds causal consumption and #41 owns the standing gate.

capabilities.label: Reciprocal families and relationships
capabilities.statement: Fibre intends relationships and families to be shared, consequential structures between independently living Threads rather than labels attached to one biography.
capabilities.limitation: Reciprocal relationship development is planned after the current M2 sequence.

capabilities.label: Thread economy with durable consequence
capabilities.statement: Fibre intends Threads to have budgets, contracts, reputation and economic opportunities that can change future possibilities.
capabilities.limitation: Economic consequence is deferred to the post-M2 foundation work.

currentWork.plainEnglish: We are preparing five completely new Threads for one clean final birth experiment. Their backgrounds and inherited dispositions are frozen before we generate their lives so we cannot tune the people after seeing who they become.
currentWork.currentStep: Run the fresh five-pair genome distinguishability ceiling. This asks whether the five frozen genomes are meaningfully distinguishable in principle before childhood generation begins.
nextSteps: Freeze and preserve the fresh genome-ceiling result, even if it is weak or fails.
Reconcile the downstream diagnostic rules to the fresh measured genome-pair topology without changing the already observed result.
Request blocking Gate-G(2) hostile review of the complete pre-life experiment.
Only if Gate-G(2) is CLEAR, generate the five replacement prior lives exactly once.
Freeze the first mechanically valid cohort and run the already-declared diagnostics.
Close #39 with CLEAR, HOLD or REDESIGN evidence; do not regenerate weak people into better ones.

truthRules: Use ordinary language first. Internal milestone names and gate labels may appear as references, not as the explanation itself.
Never use 'living Thread' as a synonym for 'generated artifact'. State whether the Thread is candidate, generated, atomically published, validated, or merely preserved evidence.
Never say a Thread 'has parents' without distinguishing live Thread parents, household caregivers, and synthetic genetic ancestors.
A failed bounded experiment remains visible as a failed experiment. Do not rewrite it into progress language that implies success.
For every positive claim, state the strongest important limitation that a reasonable reader could otherwise misunderstand.
The public website may render this contract, but insidefibre.com must not become an alternate authority for Fibre state.
